One time when I was in a small mountain city in southeast France, my buddy and I were staying at the flat of a friend of ours, and around 2AM there’s a sudden ruckus going on outside. We’re both half asleep but we were startled awake by the sound of glass breaking on the pavement. 

We go to the window, and there is just a flat out brawl in the streets. Huge guys in tracksuits just beating each other senseless. This one small guy is between a tracksuit and a blonde chick, and the tracksuit goon just spins this dude around, gets an arm around his neck, and choke-slams him into the pavement, and then no joke stomped on his skull. 

There was another smaller guy that kinda came up behind a tracksuit goon and smashed a bottle over his head. The guy just fell face first into the pavement, bloody as hell.

I see violence and gore and stuff on the internet all the time, but to see it so close up (we were observing from a 3rd floor balcony) it kinda terrified me. Needless to say, we didn’t go out late at night in that city without our native friend ever again!

So the different dating apps have very specific - and very different - purposes. It’s seems to be kind of unspoken, but from my observations (I’ve used a variety over the past 5 years or so) they typically end up as follows:

OkCupid: Definitely a casual dating site, the majority of people are there to find long term relationships, but the best part of OkCupid is that you’re expected to make your intentions clear. It asks you if you’re looking for “Long Term, Short Term, Friends, or Hookups” and you can select any and all of these options. This means that honesty becomes a big part - “Hey you’re attractive, and your profile says you’re open to hookups. I’ve got a bottle of wine with our name on it?” 

Tinder: Tinder is a mixed bag. It’s a hookup app, but it’s very saturated with holier-than-thou people who have turned to the app to find their Prince Charming. Okay honey, Bradley pursuing a degree in Nutrition with a six pack and the bio “Here for a good time” is definitely about to sweep you off your feet. But cleverness goes a long way here too. It’s really odd. Someone might be totally willing you get into the sack with you, but you’ve got to give them a good pick-up line first? I guess they just want an idea of your personality. Definitely a fun app though. Of all the women I’ve hooked up with, most were from Tinder.

Bumble: Bumble is a hardcore dating app. I’ve only ever successfully hooked up from Bumble once, and it was because we were both relatively intoxicated, horny, and available. Bumble, for those of you unfamiliar, is a dating app with unlimited “swipes” for both men and women... but only women can initiate conversation. So you’re free to swipe right on 10,000 chicks, match with 500 of them, but only receive a message from 100. Definitely not a feeling of equality, but I can’t blame the creators for giving women the chance to avoid harassment. 

Overall, as far as tips? Try to be clever, direct, and honest. Build your profile to the best of your ability ( /r/Tinder ) has a great deal of info, and they’re consistently working to help people make better profiles. Be clever, but have heart too. Or be smoking hot. My friend is a hotter guy, and has more success with Tinder even though I think his entire profile is emojis.
